localChanges: chore: update core-world-path, core-world-generator, base-unit-action-goto, civ1-unit and simple-world-path

log: `moveAlongPath` shifted the next tile off the path before trying the move. A unit short of the moves a tile costs only gets there by chance (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves`), so when the attempt failed the unit stayed put, the tile was gone, and the rest of the path started somewhere the unit wasn't. From then on nothing was adjacent: each turn dropped another tile, and the journey "finished" wherever the unit happened to be.

The tile is now only shifted once the unit is on it, so a failed attempt is retried the next turn. When no `Move` onto the next tile exists at all (an enemy unit on it, say), the journey ends straight away and the unit is handed back. Before, that happened a tile a turn, by the same draining. `passingThrough` is now `path.length > 1`, because the target is still in `path` when it's checked.

Adds the package's first tests: a failed move is retried the next turn, a path is followed to its end, and a blocked path ends the journey. Two of the three fail on the previous code. Also brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, the test step on, and test dependencies declared.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

`civ1-unit:unit/expected-movement-cost/shortfall` answers core-world-path's `ExpectedMovementCost`. With full moves `m`, a step costing `c > m` gets the unit in with a chance of `min(1, m / (c × 0.5))` per turn, and each attempt spends the turn (`not-enough-moves`). So on average the step is worth `max(m, c × 0.5)`: one turn while success is certain, and `1 / chance` turns after that. A Warrior prices mountains at 1.5 and hills at 1.

The 0.5 is now `shortfallFactor`, exported from `validateMove.ts` and used by both rules, so the chance and its price can't drift apart. The tests check the price against `validateMove`'s own outcomes across every draw.
Needs core-world-path 0.1.2, which adds the rule type.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

With `directNeighbours = false`, `se` was computed from `(x + 1, y)`, so the eight-neighbour list held the east tile twice and never the south-east one. No live caller asks for all eight, so no generated map changes.

Adds the package's first tests (every neighbour, in order, for a middle tile, the corners and each wrap seam) and brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, and the test step switched on.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#103, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

CI installs prettier 2.8.8, which parenthesises `(typeof Terrain)[]`. With `prettier:check` now actually checking (`--check`), these two files failed the build. They were never checked before, because the old script ran without `--check`.

A `Rule<[Unit, movementCost, movement], number>` that says what a step is worth to a route, on average, when it costs more than the unit's whole turn. That's when entering the tile can take more than one attempt. The rules that decide whether such a move succeeds are a ruleset's own (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves`), so the price belongs beside them and not in a path finder. A path finder asks this only for those steps, and passes `movement` in because working it out is a yield calculation.
Also brings CI up to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, and `yarn.lock` removed.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

Since 8878cb8, `generate()` ran the `MovementCost` rules for every neighbour but gave each step a cost of 1, so the search was breadth-first by step count, stopped at the first route within 110% of the straight-line distance, and never preferred a road or railroad. `Path#movementCost()` was the step count.

`generate()` is now a uniform-cost search: a binary heap of open nodes and a `Map` of the best node per tile, in place of the linear `_heap.some` and `_seen.includes` scans. Each step costs what the `MovementCost` rules say, capped at the unit's movement per turn (a one-move unit spends a turn entering hills just as it does grassland, via `not-enough-moves`), and 1 if no rule answers, as before. Ties go to fewer steps, so zero-cost rail still gives the shortest route. There is no distance heuristic, because rail costs 0. The search stops when the goal leaves the heap. `Node` gains `totalCost` and `steps`, and `movementCost()` is now the real total.
A 150-turn headless game in web-renderer (`tools/bench.js`) went from 18.5s to 14.6s.

Tests: road over mountains, rail over road, fewest steps on a cost tie, and the one-move cap for hills against a three-move unit. The duplicate `unitYield` registration is removed, because core-rule now rejects duplicate rule ids, which stopped the suite from running. CI moves to the standard setup: pnpm on Node 22, `prettier --check`, `yarn.lock` and `.yarnrc.yml` removed, and the imports that were missing from `package.json` declared.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40, civ-clone/web-renderer#66.

A step that costs more than the unit's whole turn can take more than one attempt (civ1-unit's `not-enough-moves` lets it in by chance). Capping it at a turn priced a Warrior's mountains like grassland, although it gets in only 2 times in 3. For those steps the path finder now asks core-world-path's `ExpectedMovementCost` rules, passing `(unit, movementCost, movement)`. With no rule it still costs a turn.
It's asked only for those steps, and `movement` is passed rather than recalculated: asking on every step was no slower in a 150-turn bench, but recalculating `unit.movement()` in the rule added 8s.
Tests: a priced rule sends a Warrior around five mountains (8 steps at 1 each) rather than across them (5 × 1.5 + 1), and is only asked about the mountains. Without the rule, it goes straight across.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

The tie-break compared `totalCost` exactly. Six road steps (6 × 1/3) sum to 1.9999999999999998, so a six-step road loop beat two grassland steps that cost exactly 2, contrary to "fewer steps wins ties". Costs within 1e-9 of each other now count as equal. Found by Copilot's review.
Test: from (1, 1) to (3, 1), two grassland steps are chosen over a six-step road loop of the same cost. It fails before this change.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.

cb340cd compared costs with a 1e-9 tolerance. That isn't transitive: with (cost, steps) A = (2, 3), B = (2 + 0.75e-9, 2), C = (2 + 1.5e-9, 1), it says B < A, C < B and A < C, and a binary heap needs a strict weak order, so it could pop the wrong node first. Each node now carries `costKey`, its total cost rounded to millionths, and nodes compare by `(costKey, steps)`, which is transitive. Six road steps (1.9999999999999998) and 2 still share a key, so the float-tie test still holds. Found by Copilot's review.
Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#40.
